XI.}}|{{sc|to the corinthians.}}|449}}</noinclude>{{verse|chapter=11|verse=4|align=float}}† Euery man praying or prophecying vvith his head couered: di{{ls}}hone{{ls}}teth his head. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=5|align=float}}† But {{sup|‖}} euery vvoman praying or prophecying vvith her head not couered: di{{ls}}hone{{ls}}teth her head: for it is al one as if {{ls}}he vvere made balde. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=6|align=float}}† For if a vvoman be not couered, let her be polled. but if it be a foule thing for a vvoman to be polled or made balde: let her couer her head. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=7|align=float}}† The man truely ought not to couer his head, becau{{ls}}e he is the image and glorie of God, but the vvoman is the glorie of the man. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=8|align=float}}† For the man is not of the vvoman, but the vvoman of the man. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=9|align=float}}† For * {{outside L|''Gen. 2, 21.''}} the man vvas not created for the vvoman, but the vvoman for the man. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=10|align=float}}† (Therfore ought the vvoman to haue povver vpon her head for the Angels.) {{verse|chapter=11|verse=11|align=float}}† But yet neither the man vvithout the vvoman: nor the vvoman vvithout the man, in our Lord. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=12|align=float}}† For as the vvoman is of the man, {{ls}}o al{{ls}}o the man by the vvoman: but al things of God. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=13|align=float}}† Your {{ls}}elues iudge: doth it become a vvoman not couered to pray vnto God? {{verse|chapter=11|verse=14|align=float}}† Neither doth nature it {{ls}}elf teach you, that a man in deede if he nouri{{ls}}h his heare, it is an ignominie for him: {{verse|chapter=11|verse=15|align=float}}† but if a vvoman nouri{{ls}}h her heare, it is a glorie for her, becau{{ls}}e heare is giuen her for a veile? {{verse|chapter=11|verse=16|align=float}}† But if any man {{ls}}eeme to be contentious, vve haue no {{ls}}uch {{sup|‖}} cu{{ls}}tome, nor the {{outside L|''`churches''}}`{{sc|Chvrch}}' of God.

{{verse|chapter=11|verse=17|align=float}}† And this I commaund: not prai{{ls}}ing it that you come together not to better, but to vvor{{ls}}e. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=18|align=float}}† {{outside R|The Epi{{ls}}tle vpon Maundy Thur{{ls}}day.}}Fir{{ls}}t in deede vvhen you come together into the Church, I heare that there are {{ls}}chi{{ls}}mes among you, and in part I beleeue it. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=19|align=float}}† For {{sup|‖}} there mu{{ls}}t be here{{ls}}ies al{{ls}}o: that they al{{ls}}o vvhich are approued, may be made manife{{ls}}t among you. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=20|align=float}}† Vvhen you come therfore together in one, is it not novv to eate {{sup|‖}} our Lordes {{ls}}upper. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=21|align=float}}† For euery one taketh his ovvne {{ls}}upper before to eate. And one certes is an hungred, and an other is drunke. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=22|align=float}}† Vvhy, haue you not hou{{ls}}es to eate and drinke in? or contemne ye the Church of God: and confound them that haue not? Vvhat {{ls}}hal I {{ls}}ay to you? prai{{ls}}e I you in this? I do not prai{{ls}}e you.
